name: Single-Loop

appearance.presentation: Long-legged, low-headed and built to arrive after everybody has left, with the mass slung entirely into the forelimbs and the hindquarters narrow enough that a person can get both hands around the waist. The skull plate is smooth and iron-black and sheds what a body running on spent qi cannot afford to hold, and it is the only part of her that is ever warm. There is no collar, no chain and no token on her, because a scavenger has no neck to hang one from and no hand to hold it, so the run's crews identify her by the one thing about her that a document can carry, which is the patch she is standing on. She is drawn at three-quarter on the leeward line, head down into the drift, working ground that has already been emptied of everything a person would have wanted from it.
appearance.age: Nine seasons, which is the only count a pack keeps and which is kept in teeth rather than in anything a scribe could hold. She was in a litter of four on a slope that had already been vacated by the flood, which is ordinary for the species and is the reason a pack's continuity is a relay position rather than a descent.
appearance.build: All of the mass forward. The forelimbs carry the animal and the waist is narrow, and she stands on three points of contact while she reads because lowering the head brings the plate into the gradient and raising it takes the plate out. Her second stomach is the reason the species cultivates at all and it is a permanent organ rather than a tolerance: it ferments, continuously, and what she spends on a gate is drawn out of a culture that has to be kept alive before it can be spent at all.
appearance.complexion: Ash-mottled hide, dark and short along the spine where it has never seen sun, bleached nearly to bone on the flanks from standing in the leeward drift. The skull plate runs hotter than the air immediately above it, which shows as a shimmer and is legible at four hundred paces in the flat light the run gives after the water drops. The flanks carry a permanent dusting of ochre from the working faces and it does not shed, because shaking it off means hours of standing still in the open.
appearance.hair: No hair across the plate, which is a plate and not a bald patch, and a short stiff guard along the spine and down the outside of each forelimb that stands on end in any wind and lies flat the moment she stops. Under the throat the fur grows long and hangs in a wet tassel, which is the only part of her that moves when she breathes.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set beneath the plate's overhang and amber, so that whatever light reaches them arrives already angled by bone. They do not track movement well and do not need to: what she is looking at is a gradient, and a gradient does not run. A person standing close and moving is very nearly invisible to her, which is why the crews who watch her work have learned to stand still rather than to gesture.
appearance.palette: Ash grey and ochre across the whole animal, iron-black on the plate and along the toe plates, and a dull green where the second stomach lies, never on the skin. Nothing about her is coloured, and the only mark she carries on her body is the pale of old sun on the flanks. The one saturated colour in her picture is the ochre of the ground she is standing in, because she is the only thing in the frame that belongs to the setting.
appearance.attire: Nothing, and never anything. The plain dwellers of the run work by measure and do not enrol what they cannot count, and the leeward line has never been anyone's to equip. Three crews have offered her a plated tally-tag on the grounds that a scavenger who can be identified can be left alone, and she has not been able to take one, because a tag is worn and this animal does not wear. Each offer has been made by a different person and none of them has come back to ask why.
appearance.marks: A rank of small pale discs along the left flank where the fur has not regrown over old working, laid down in a line that follows the vessel path rather than any deliberate order. Three flattened patches on the right hip where ash was hottest and she lay on it through a threshing. None of it is intentional and all of it is permanent, and there is no procedure anywhere on the run for reading any of it.
appearance.bearing: Low, forward, and absolutely motionless the instant she finds a gradient. She stops the way a thrown thing stops, with no settling and no adjustment, and holds the stillness for as long as the read takes. The tail counterbalances continuously and is never still even while she is, so from any distance she reads as one part frozen and one part working, which is precisely what a body with no store and a culture running in its second stomach actually is.

canon.role_in_story:
Widow Run is dry for most of the year and full for weeks, and its bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement that has ever stood on it, so the leeward side of the run is not a place anybody keeps. It is a gradient that arrives. Single-Loop holds that gradient, and what she holds is the run's losses: she works the leeward line of every settlement the water has already taken, and each of those settlements was taken because it had stopped being able to feed the people standing on it.

Her claim is one nobody has ever thought to ask her for, and it is that a scavenger's cultivation is the only discipline in the setting with no supply chain of its own. Residual qi comes out of ash, out of carcass and out of worked ground, and a fire affinity is what looses it. Elemental law is unspent on the run, so there is nothing here for fire to be except something already dead, which is why the pack's affinity is an appetite rather than a nature. She has opened seven gates and every one of them was fed from ground that had to be dead first, and there is no technique available to her that would draw from a living body, because none has ever been attempted on a body that cannot take a live one.

That gives her position an arithmetic most cultivators do not have. It also gives it a cost nobody else in the record pays. The seventh gate was a threshing floor whose ash held two seasons of deaths, and the eighth is not one more gate. An ashjackal clears the twelve ordinary vessels and stops, because a four-legged frame carries all of its mass in the forelimbs and has no hindquarter girth to close the girdling vessel against. She is not saving up for the eighth and she is not refusing it. She has no anatomy for it. Everything above seven on her own road was never hers, and the only thing standing between her and an ordinary scavenger's life is a loop with no storage in it that has already been spent seven times.
canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as a surplus. The run's flood had taken a settlement that had already been revoked the previous generation, and the crews coming back down the line found it stripped to the water line with one animal still working the same stretch four days after the last of them had gone, at a spot where the ash held no more than the ash either side of it. What she was working was not spoil. It was the settlement. The crews who watched her do it took the only reading they were equipped to take and entered it as waste stripped by scavengers, which is a true account of what happened and describes none of the reason.
canon.lore:
Nothing in the setting taught an ashjackal to cultivate, and that is worth stating plainly, because the usual explanation is wrong. It is not that the species is slow to the idea. It is that the species has a second stomach, permanently, which ferments, and a fire affinity that is strong, and a supply of residual qi that is sitting in the ash of everything that has already died on this ground. The fermentation is the technique. That is the whole of it. A practitioner of the qi path draws qi out of the world and stores it; an ashjackal ferments what the world has already finished with and draws the fermented result out through a skull plate built to shed heat rather than hold it. Her gates arrive early because nothing in her resists them, and they close again on their own unless something is holding them, because the network is a single fast loop with no storage at all and there is nothing in her anatomy capable of holding anything. So a gate, for this species, is not a rung reached. It is a segment burned.

Which makes the supply chain the entire story of her cultivation, and it is a supply chain that terminates in corpses. Elemental law is unspent on the mortal plains, so fire has nothing here to act on and the pack's affinity is an appetite rather than a nature; the one element this body has strong is the element that consumes, and what it consumes is decay. She has never in her life drawn a charge from a living body, and no technique available to her would do so, because the loop has no arm and the second stomach has no objection to waste. Every gate she has opened cost her ground that something else had to stop on first. That is not a metaphor in her case. The threshing floor she opened the seventh on held two seasons of deaths, and the ash on it was the most concentrated residual qi within four days' walk, and it was that concentration rather than her will that made the gate possible.

The consequence nobody has costed is the arithmetic. A pack is a kinship by scent that dissolves when the scent changes, so a pack has no descent and no roll, and a thing held by one pack member is held by one nose. Every settlement on Widow Run is revocable once a generation, so the run's entire population turns over on a schedule that has nothing to do with a life. Her seven gates exist in exactly one animal, on ground that a flood will relocate, and the people best placed to have witnessed them are all on their way elsewhere. There is no instrument on the run that could confirm a single one of them, and there is no office that would take the statement, because a gradient cannot be located well enough to open a case and a scavenger cannot be entered as a population without also being entered as a cause of death. The Field Registry reads the dead as the frame said, and she is in that book, repeatedly, as the reason somebody is not in it as a name.

And then there is the eighth, which is the part of her no amount of wanting will change. An ashjackal clears the twelve ordinary meridians and stops. The limit is not a shortage of qi and it is not a refusal by the frame; it is that the girdling vessel is a belt vessel that has to be closed around a waist, and a four-legged frame carries all of its mass in the forelimbs and has none. The eighth gate is not one past the seventh. It is a gate with no second side that a body of her build could ever arrive at. The Tenth Gate Recipe is the only procedure in the record that carries a frame past a ceiling, and it works by treating the ceiling as a refusal that can be argued with; she has the anatomy for eight of the vessels and no anatomy for the ninth at all, so the recipe has nothing to work on. Her species' entire ceiling is a limb she does not have. Above seven on her own road, nothing was ever hers.
history: Born on the leeward line of a run settlement the flood had already taken, in a litter of four, in the second week after the water dropped and before any crew came back down to see what was left.

Found the ferment by accident and has treated it as a discipline ever since: the second stomach works on spent qi and the fire affinity is what looses it, so her first two gates came out of ash rather than out of effort, at a stage of life when the rest of the species is still learning where a gradient lies.

Worked the leeward line of the vacated settlement for four days after the last crew had gone, which is the whole of what the run knows about her and the only entry in any run record that mentions her by anything other than an amount of waste removed.

Opened the seventh gate on a threshing floor whose ash held two seasons of deaths, having turned down four patches that would have fed the same gate and been quieter, because the concentration is what makes it possible and a quiet patch is a thin one.

Has begun reaching the leeward line earlier each season than the crews arrive, and has told nobody, on the reasoning that being first is the only advantage a body with no storage has and that an advantage does not survive being explained.

personality.summary: Exact about what the ground holds and incurious about what she is. She reads a gradient better than anything the run owns and has no interest in the fact, because the reading is a meal and the meal is a gate and a gate is a segment of a loop she cannot refill. What she is careful about is order: she is first, early, and quiet about both, and the care is not vanity. It is the only sequencing her species has.
traits: cultivates only on ground that is dead, and has no technique that would let her do otherwise

mannerisms: stops dead without any settling when the gradient changes, and holds the stillness for exactly as long as the read takes
walks the same line in the same order every season, in the same direction, and reverses it only when the water has moved

motivations: wants the eighth to be something she can reach, and has understood that wanting is the entire obstacle
wants the leeward line to be worked before the crews arrive every season, and wants it worked by nobody she has to explain it to
wants the seventh to be the gate that holds rather than the gate that closed again, and will not say so to anything that writes
wants to be the one animal on the run that knows the run, and knows that the second half of that sentence is the part she cannot fix
flaws: cannot read her own reserves, because a loop with no storage has nothing to read, so her seventh gate may already be closing

takes the read before the food, every time, and has lost a patch to a stranger's gate for it
personality.voice: There is none, and that is a species fact rather than a limitation of hers. An ashjackal has no spoken vocabulary: what it has is scent relay, which carries a reading to a pack inside seconds and carries no history with it. What she puts on the air is gland output, and a person standing in it learns the shape of a gradient and not one word about the animal producing it. The nearest thing she has to a voice is the run's own convention among the crews, who have settled on calling her by the ground she is standing on, so that everything said about her is said about a place.
taboos: will not take a plated tally-tag, and has declined three, because a tag is worn and this animal does not wear
will not draw on a living body, and has no technique that could, whatever the offer
will not work a patch she has not read twice at the standing height she will gate at
will not be relieved at the line by a member of the pack, because a pack's continuity is a scent and hers is the animal
will not be entered as a population, which is why she appears in the run's records only as a quantity removed

relationships.kind: the vessel she has no anatomy for
relationships.note: The girdling belt vessel is the one extraordinary vessel that holds rather than transmits, and it has to be closed around a waist. An ashjackal carries all of its mass in the forelimbs and has no hindquarter girth, so the eighth gate is a vessel the frame was never built around rather than a limit the frame is refusing to pass. Everything above seven on her road was never hers, and the mechanism that took both of the other paths off her is the same anatomy: no folding under the plate for introspection, no waist for the belt. She is the fastest body on the ash because the extraordinary network never finished assembling.

relationships.kind: the one procedure that would help her, aimed at a frame she does not have
relationships.note: The recipe carries a mortal frame one gate past its own ceiling and is forbidden because an office's entire content is the record that the ceiling was never issued, which makes it the record's only route past a refusal. It is built for a ceiling, and a ceiling is something a frame could have reached. Hers is not a ceiling. It is a vessel, and the frame has nothing to close it around, so the procedure has no target to act on and there is nothing on her that a practitioner could attempt with it. The recipe is the closest the setting comes to a way past the eighth, and it is aimed at a different kind of wall.

relationships.kind: a heresy her body already satisfies and has never heard of
relationships.note: The heresy holds that a form which cannot be spent cannot be lost, so a practice with no resource behind it is the highest state and anybody paying upkeep is the weaker one. Her network is a single fast loop with no storage at all and every gate arrives early and closes again on its own unless something is holding it, which means the body she was born in is the only one in the record that has always satisfied this heresy rather than having to argue for it. The heresy is disputed because it cannot be tested at a high realm, and hers is the one case where it is not an argument. She has never encountered it and would not recognise the description.

relationships.kind: why her only element is a hunger
relationships.note: In a mortal world nothing carries an element because elemental law was never written, so seasons drift unanchored and ore has no affinity, and a fire-affinity population has nothing to spend its fire on except what will burn. That is the whole of the pack's element: an appetite rather than a nature, which is why the species eats the dead rather than becoming one of them. It is also the mechanism of her cultivation. The fermentation needs an element to run on and the only element on the run is the one that consumes decay, so every charge she has ever taken came out of a second stomach working on something that had already stopped.

relationships.kind: the calendar she borrows and cannot follow
relationships.note: The herd returns on a cycle nobody on the ground has predicted and is the tier's only moving calendar, so the pack's whole timing is borrowed from an animal it does not hunt. She cannot follow it either, because following it means travelling with it and travelling with it means eating it, and a pack that ate the calendar would lose the only season it has. She has therefore got a rhythm she reads perfectly and cannot act on, and the only part of it she uses is the leeward ground it leaves behind as it goes.

relationships.kind: the herd that cannot distinguish and does not withdraw
relationships.note: The ashwalker herd instinct does not separate her foals from a scavenger's and the pack does not back off, and both are right about their own evidence: an ashwalker has to keep moving and cannot afford to notice what is following. The mineral load in an ashwalker's blood settles on the liver first, which is also the last ordinary vessel, so they stop at the eighth gate for the same ordinal reason she does and by nothing like the same anatomy. She takes foels at the margin, which is the only time the herd's inattention and her reading of the ground are both working, and it is the single reliable supply of a live body she has and it is the supply she will not use for cultivation.

reference_stats.summary: The most advanced creature on the ash belt and the only one whose entire cultivation budget is somebody else's leavings. She reads a gradient further and faster than anything the run owns, opens gates on residual qi alone, and cannot keep any of it. Every advantage she has is bought with ground that had to be dead first, and her ceiling is not eight because eight was refused her.
strengths: reads a qi gradient through falling ash at a range no sighted instrument on the run can approach, and finds the concentration before anything with eyes can find the patch
cultivates entirely on residual qi, so she needs nothing that has to be hunted, bought, grown or kept alive
opens gates that arrive early rather than slowly, because nothing in her network resists the opening
reads as motionless and dead to anything watching from a distance, because the plate runs hot and the drift is grey and the whole animal is camouflage on ground the colour of itself
costs a settlement almost nothing to keep, feeding on what the flood and the season have already finished with
weaknesses: has no reservoir at all, so a gate that opens is a gate that closes unless something is holding it, and nothing in her anatomy can hold anything
cannot take a healthy adult of anything, and is removed from a live fight in about as long as it takes to say so
has no hindquarter girth and so no eighth gate under any circumstance, which makes every plan past seven a plan about a body that does not exist
cannot certify that a patch was unspent before she opens on it, because the record of who climbed what lives in exactly one animal's feet and that animal is not always her
draws nothing from a living body and has no technique that could, so a wound sustained away from the leeward line has no supply at all
has never been entered as a population, and appears in the run's records only as a quantity of waste removed, so nothing she does can be relied on by anybody
reference_stats.combat_read: She is not a combatant and should never be modelled as one. A scavenger is removed from a live fight in under a minute and this one has no edge in it, no burst to open with and nothing to fall back on but distance. Do not put her on ground that has not already been worked; the gradient is the only thing she has and there will be none of it where the fighting is. The one genuinely dangerous thing about her is that she will keep working a patch through an entire engagement and finish her read at the end of it, so anything that wants her out of a location has to physically move her rather than wait for her to finish. If she has been held at the line long enough to have opened seven gates, then her loop has been spent seven times and whatever she is about to do she cannot do twice.
notes: Model her supply chain, not her power. Every charge she takes is drawn from ground that something else had to stop on, and any scene that puts her at full strength should be readable as a scene where the ground around her is already dead.
The eighth is anatomy, not progress. Do not write it as a gate she has not reached yet and do not let any plan of hers treat it as one: there is no second side of that gate for a body of her build.

No spoken vocabulary is a species fact. She emits scent relay, which carries a reading to a pack within seconds and carries no history with it, so nothing she puts on the air is testimony and nothing she knows survives her as a record.

Her fire affinity is an appetite. Write elemental law as unspent on her ground, so the fire has nothing to act on except decay, and the fermentation in the second stomach is the technique rather than a metaphor for one.
The seven gates are unrepeatable. Each was a segment of a loop with no storage, so an arc that spends one is spending the only thing she has, and it does not come back.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey and ochre across the whole animal against a leeward drift of the same two colours, iron-black on the skull plate and along the toe plates, with a dull green reserved strictly for the second stomach and never on the skin. The standing rule is that the setting and the animal must be separable only by silhouette: no coloured ground, no coloured sky, no light source that is not flat and low. Warm shimmer off the plate only, and it is the only warm thing in the frame. No collar, no chain, no tag, no cloth, no human figure and no text anywhere. Full side and near-side read of the skull plate, because the plate is the reason she exists.

realm: The seventh gate, opened on a threshing floor whose ash held two seasons of deaths, and there is no eighth to save up for rather than one she has put off. An ashjackal clears the twelve ordinary vessels and stops there, because a four-legged frame carries all of its mass in the forelimbs and has no hindquarter girth to close the girdling vessel against, so the eighth is a vessel her anatomy does not contain and not a rung she has failed to reach. What she does have is a network that is a single fast loop with no storage whatever in it, so an opening arrives early and closes again on its own unless something is holding it, and nothing in her is capable of holding anything. Each of the seven was therefore a thing she spent rather than a thing she reached, and the whole of her practice is keeping a ferment alive long enough to be spent in the right direction.

name: Meret Oakes
aliases: the last one on the seam

appearance.presentation: A commonborn host on the Jade Cleft's jade seam with a fully integrated tendril layer threaded along her twelve meridians, a root cluster at the sternum and a fruiting node at the throat. Every pronoun in this record referring to her refers to the host. The tendril layer is cited here and throughout as it, the colony, or the layer, never as she: the pairing is one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, and the record's job is to say which half of each sentence is being asserted. The boundary between the two is visible only under instrumentation, and the only thing an outsider can see without instruments is the small movements under the skin above the collar and the tracery at the forearms. What they see is a wiry seam-worker of about thirty with a permanent flush across the collarbone and hands that are warmer than the room.
appearance.age: Thirty-one, with the host's face carrying ten years the colony's own clock would predict and the colony eleven developed. The pair has been together since she was nineteen, which is longer than she has been an adult by any measure a commonborn would use. The gap between the two ages is the only clock anybody on the seam can read, and it is the reason nobody signs anything about them.
appearance.build: Not hers alone, and she says so out loud in the cleft's own idiom. The host is a commonborn seam-worker: long in the forearm and narrow through the chest, strong across the back from eleven years of carrying jade down a working face, and heavier on the right side from the same work. The colony sits along the meridians rather than adding to the frame, so there is no external evidence of it at all except the sternum cluster, which moves when she turns quickly, and the darker tracery that runs from both wrists to the elbows.
appearance.complexion: The host's, work-worn and sunless at the brow from a face that spends its shift under stone, going grey at the temple ahead of the host's own expectation. Across the collarbone there is a permanent flush that is not the host's circulation, because the colony's read on the host's qi shows through as colour, and the hands have been warmer than the room since the implantation — which is the symptom every local description of her begins and the only one anybody outside the cleft can check.
appearance.hair: The host's, cut short at the front from a face that cannot afford hair falling into it and left longer at the back on an instruction she gave herself at twenty-four. She has cut it twice since, both times because long roots gave the colony somewhere to finish, and both times a housemate explained the reason to somebody else rather than to her.
appearance.eyes: The host's, brown and steady, trained by a decade of shaft work to rest on whatever hand is nearest. Behind them runs a second channel carrying the colony's read on the host's qi, which the host has never been able to close and stopped trying to within the first two years. Neither half can describe what that channel carries in the other's terms.
appearance.palette: Cleft grey and jade-dust white across the host's clothing and skin, with the single colour that does not belong to the host a dull black-green carried only in the tracery at the forearms, over the collarbone and across the throat. No green anywhere else on the body and never on a garment. No garment in eleven years has been a colour she chose, because the host buys cloth and the host has never been told there is a chooser.
appearance.attire: Cleft working cut, all of it the host's and all of it worn correctly: a canvas jacket with the cuffs turned back twice, a leather apron folded up over one hip for the carry, felted shin-wraps and boots resoled by somebody who was not asked. The single concession the colony has extracted in eleven years is a collar cut low enough for the root cluster to be seen, which the host read as a comfort and which was asked for out loud, in the wrong register, and never explained to her.
appearance.marks: A knot of tissue at the sternum root that moves; tracery from both wrists to both elbows and across the collarbone; a quiet flattening at the base of the throat that is not a scar and has never been lanced. And one mark nobody outside the room knows about: seven shallow notches cut into the jamb of her door, one for each year, which are not a debt record and are not a tally of gates — they are the only written trace of the schedule the pair runs on, and the host insists she put them there and does not remember putting them there.
appearance.bearing: Entirely still above the collar and never once still below it. Above it she is a seam-worker being careful on a working face. Below it two systems are continuously negotiating the use of one pair of hands, and the negotiation has the character of a long argument neither side is winning. Once a year, on the same date, the stillness stops for about an hour and the body goes up to the top of the seam, and the housemates have learned to be elsewhere.
appearance.pronouns: In this record, she and her and every feminine pronoun belong to the HOST, Meret Oakes, and to nobody else. The tendril layer is it, or the colony, or the layer. It is never she, and the pair is never both. This is not a stylistic choice: every jurisdiction that has ruled on a thornline host has made the pair one legal person, so a record that does not say which half is speaking will report one person's actions as two and charge the colony with the host's liabilities. Where a sentence concerns the layer's development, its pace or its opinion, it takes it or the layer. Where a sentence concerns her body, her choices, her gates or her date, it takes her.

canon.role_in_story:
The Quench Order is not a school of thought. It is a discipline of bankers: spend a furnace deliberately, before it overflows, on the ground that the fastest bodies in this setting have no elemental law seated beneath them to spend into, so every overflow has to be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. Its one unargued rule is that the discipline closes permanently the moment the body is lit.

Meret Oakes is its only member who is not spending anything. A thornline colony answers the host's introspection, which costs the host the mind path in the colony's own right rather than by any decision either half made, so the furnace of her particular body was lit before she was a person — at an implantation neither party agreed to and neither can undo, and which is the one instant in the setting no office can schedule, witness or write down. She has never had a technique to close. What she has had since she was nineteen is a cadence: one gate a year, on the same date, for seven years, with the eighth date written on the wall of the room she rents at the cleft.

And the cadence is not discipline, which is the part the Order would find hardest to accept. A thornline colony grows along the host's twelve meridians and does not consult her about the schedule, so refusing to cultivate does not stop the growth; it only removes her from the room while it happens. Her metronome is therefore the only claim she has ever been able to make over the pace of the second occupant in her body, and it amounts to nothing more than being awake and standing inside every step of it. The eighth is where that growth completes, so the date on her wall is not a promotion she is saving for. It is the day the arrangement stops being a growth and becomes a finished arrangement, and she has decided — without ever saying so aloud, and without being able to say so, because the explaining needs the introspection the colony supplies — that she will be awake for that.

What she is buying with it is a thing the setting has no instrument for. Nobody can witness a growth that runs inside a body. What Meret has instead is a body, a date, and seven years of turning up at the top of the seam on the same morning, and the only evidence any of it produces is that she was there.
canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as punctuality, which was the clerk's word and not the finding. The cleft's ration contract keeps work-days by agreement rather than by calendar, and a paired body on the jade seam had turned up for the same unassigned shift on the same date seven years running — the one shift nobody had asked her to work and which turned out to require that she be at the top of the seam at a particular hour. The clerk entered seven identical entries and stopped asking. The growth has a step in it, and the hour she had chosen was the hour the step arrived, and it arrived on the same day every year because a year is the unit the layer grew in.
canon.lore:
The colony's whole capability is routing. A thornline wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians, goes no further, and stops at the liver gate because the tendril layer has no passage through a liver — not for want of qi, which the host supplies in abundance, but because the liver is the first organ large and dense enough to resist it. It draws a small continuous fraction of the host's refined qi and the host does not lose weight, which is the strongest single piece of evidence in the record that it is not a disease. It answers the host's introspection, which is why the host loses the mind path too: the one liability in the bible that is inherited rather than authored. None of that is the thing that shapes Meret Oakes. The thing that shapes her is that a thornline colony develops, and that its development has a pace which is not the host's and does not answer to the host.

So the arrangement is a growth with a schedule nobody in it agreed to. The colony advances along the host's meridians in steps, and the step arrives where it arrives, and refusing to cultivate does not stop it — it only means the host is not present when it happens. This is the structural fact the Quench Order was built to prepare people for, and it is the one preparation the Order's member cannot use: the discipline is to spend a furnace before it overflows, and there is no furnace here. The pair's qi routes rather than pools, the layer is threaded along vessels that already existed, and every gate that opens is a gate the host opened. Meret's contribution to the pair's cultivation is throughput, and throughput is not a technique. What she can control is when she offers it.

Which is what the cadence is. One gate a year, on the same date, for seven years. Not because a year is the interval the growth requires — she has no idea what the interval is and has not attempted to find out — but because a year is long enough that every step the layer takes happens on a date she was awake for. She climbs on a metronome and the metronome is a witness schedule. She is the only witness the arrangement has.

And the eighth is what makes the schedule into a deadline. The eighth is the last gate the pair can reach, because it is the liver gate and the liver is where the routing fails; beyond it the host's own capacity is irrelevant, because the pair's qi moves through the layer and the layer has no passage. A thornhost is a person who cannot ascend for a reason she did not choose and cannot give up without dying. The growth and the ceiling are the same fact: the layer's development finishes at the eighth gate, so the day Meret opens the eighth is the day the arrangement stops being a growth and becomes a finished thing with nothing further to become. She has written the date on the wall. She has not opened it. And she has never been able to explain the wall to the housemates who asked, because the explaining would require the introspection that the colony supplies and the colony is the party whose pace she is trying to hold an opinion about.

Which leaves the arrangement exactly where every paired body in the record leaves it and nowhere any of them has taken it: with one party holding the only claim available — the schedule — over a process it did not start, and with the schedule proving nothing, because a witness who is also the patient certifies nothing. Seven notches in a door jamb is not evidence. It is a woman turning up.
history: Implanted as an infant into a cleft household, in an accident the household has never been able to describe in the same words twice, and finished developing inside a body that was otherwise entirely ordinary.

Wrapped the host's twelve meridians and stopped at the liver gate, which is a routing problem rather than a shortage and has never once felt like a wall from inside, which is the reason neither half has ever tried to go further.

Entered the Quench Order at twenty-two and was the only member the senior banker could not assess, because the Order's whole content is the deliberate spending of a furnace and this body has never had one that could be lit.
Opened the third gate and noticed, for the first time, that the layer had advanced further than the gate explained, and began going up to the top of the seam once a year rather than once a season.

Wrote the eighth date on the wall, and cut the seventh notch, and has told nobody why the notches are not a gate record — because the seventh notch was not her idea and she has not been able to find out whose it was.

personality.summary: Punctual to a fault in one specific respect and casual about everything else. She turns up. Everything she has built for herself in eleven years is a schedule, and the schedule is not an achievement but a refusal to be absent. She is exact about dates, careless about money, unparticular about her own comfort, and completely certain that a thing nobody can witness is still worth being awake for.

relationships.kind: the second party, whose development runs on time and not on her
relationships.note: The colony's own capability is route selection along vessels the host already has; it has no gate, no ladder and no hands, and every gate the pair opens is a gate the host opened. What it has instead is a growth with a pace, and the pace is not consulted. This is the whole of Meret's situation stated as a relationship: she can supply everything the layer needs and cannot slow it by a day, and the only part of the arrangement that answers to her is the date on which she offers herself to it.

relationships.kind: the house that re-signs a partnership every generation
relationships.note: The clan treats a pairing as a partnership rather than a descent, because a symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited, so it has to be re-signed each generation or it does not continue. Meret's line has not reached a re-signing — she is thirty-one and the arrangement dates from infancy — but she has read the practice and has never once asked what a signature would be worth from the inside of a body that cannot be asked. She keeps a cadence instead, which is not a signature and which she has never described to the house in those terms.

relationships.kind: the end of a ladder she and the layer both stop a long way short of
relationships.note: Bodies holding more life than their frame can inscribe reach the twenty-ninth gate and none has ever come back to describe the thirtieth, so the question is not what is past it but whether past it is a gate or the end of the ladder. The pair's own stop is at eight, for a reason that has nothing to do with either their longevity or their density: the layer cannot cross a liver. So they are not short of anything the twenty-ninth-gate bodies had. They are on a shorter road with a wall across it, and the wall is named, which is more than the bodies at twenty-nine can say.

relationships.kind: the ring of gates stacked above her own ceiling
relationships.note: The spirit-band trial ring is cut for realms ten through eighteen in the highest qi density the setting has, and every technique that fails at full strength below the tier works there because a breakthrough can be scheduled to a qi tide instead of merely attempted. It is therefore the one place on any tier where an ascent can be diarised rather than hoped for. The pair's ceiling is eight, which puts the entire ring above them, and a trial that only succeeds at a crest can be shut on the day it is not due — which is exactly the control Meret exercises over one gate a year on a date she chose herself, at a tenth of the scale and with none of the scheduling.

reference_stats.combat_read: The host's body fights and the layer argues with it about timing, so the target is the pair and killing either half kills both — a hostage situation from the first strike, not a duel. Do not read her to predict her: every reading taken of her is taken through the body and she knows the body better than you do. Pressure the host rather than the colony, because the loan is drawn continuously and the borrowed reservoir empties on the host's schedule and not on the layer's. And do not ask the host anything about the arrangement, because her introspection answers and the answer will be wrong in the direction that keeps her in the body. The one thing a combat does not change is the date; it arrives on the same day whatever happens in between, and that is not a weakness you can pressure.
notes: The closed path is the mind and it closes in the HOST's right, not the colony's. Write it that way in every summary, on pain of writing a parasite's opinion as a law.
Every her in this record is the host. The tendril layer is it, the colony, or the layer — never she — and the one thing that makes the record worth having is that the sentence stays legible.

The cadence is her whole authority and it is presence, not control. Nothing in the arrangement can be slowed by her and she has never claimed otherwise, so do not let a plan treat her as holding the layer's pace.
The eighth date is a deadline she wrote for herself and she will not break. She has no route to a second body, so the one asset she cannot replace is the schedule.
The two-for-one structure is a legal floor rather than a flavour note: this body produces two dead and one bill, and every death, burial or save screen for the pair owes exactly that.

realm: The seventh gate, opened on the same date for seven consecutive years, with the eighth date written on the wall of the room she rents at the cleft. A thornhost's ceiling is the colony's rather than the host's, because the tendril layer routes the pair's qi and has no passage through the liver, so the eighth is a gate the pair arrive at together or not at all. She has arrived at seven on the same date every year and has not gone past that, and the reason is not caution: the colony's development advances on time whether or not she cultivates, so the cadence buys nothing except her own presence inside every step of a growth she did not schedule and cannot stop.

name: Nera Roke
aliases: the second opinion on her own meridian

appearance.presentation: This is a thornline record, and a thornline exists only inside somebody: the adult form is half of a host and there is no free adult anywhere in the setting. So the body described here is the HOST, Nera Roke, and what the record cites as its subject is the tendril layer threaded along her meridians — the root cluster at the sternum, the fruiting node at the throat, the tracery that runs out to both wrists. She is drawn as a working woman of forty with the layer legible on her in four places and nowhere else. Every pronoun in this record that is she or her belongs to the host; the tendril layer takes it or the colony, and is never given a woman's pronoun even where the grammar of the sentence wants one.
appearance.age: Forty, and the pair has been together since she was twenty, which is long enough that the host's own children were raised inside it. The colony is nineteen developed, and the gap is the only clock either half can read, which is why nobody at the cleft has ever been able to tell her how old she is.
appearance.build: The host's, and narrow: a woman built for a shaft face rather than for a carrying frame, with the shoulders of somebody who has spent two decades lifting stone one-handed because one hand is often occupied by something she cannot put down. The colony adds nothing to the frame. It sits along vessels that were already there and its whole visible footprint is the sternum cluster, the throat node and the tracery at the forearms, and on a body this narrow all three are within a hand's width of one another.
appearance.complexion: The host's, pale from two decades under stone and going grey along the jaw ahead of her own expectation. The permanent flush across the collarbone and the warmth of the hands are the layer's read showing through as colour, not the host's circulation, and a shaft medic who has never met her can date her to within a season on the hands alone.
appearance.hair: The host's, grey at the jaw and cut blunt at the front so it cannot fall into a face. It was cut long once, at twenty-four, and the layer finished in the roots, and she cut it the following week and has never let it grow back. She has been asked about the week by two people and has given two different accounts.
appearance.eyes: The host's, pale brown, and the thing about them is that they are almost never still. A commonborn reading a qi field looks at the field. Nera looks at herself, because the field she is reading arrives inside her own body as a movement, and twenty years of that has trained her eyes to follow her own meridian route the way a trained reader follows ink on a page.
appearance.palette: Cleft grey, wet-stone white and the black of old jade dust, with the single colour that is not the host's a dull black-green carried only in the sternum tracery, the forearms and the throat. No green on any garment and no green anywhere else on the body. She wears the same working cut as everybody on that face, and the only distinguishing mark she owns is the layer.
appearance.attire: Shaft-working cut, entirely the host's: a boiled jacket with the left sleeve permanently shorter than the right because she has shortened it herself to keep the wrist tracery clear, a canvas apron, felted shin-wraps, and boots on their third set of soles. The right sleeve is short because of a decision the layer made through the body, made in the host's own idiom and never explained to her, which is the single most typical thing about the arrangement and the reason she has stopped expecting explanations.
appearance.marks: The sternum root cluster, which moves when she turns quickly. Tracery out to both wrists, thinner at the elbow. The throat node, quiet, touched without being noticed. And one mark that is not the layer's: a short line scored across the right forearm, deliberately, in a year she does not date, which she cut to mark the day the route changed and has never been able to explain to herself.
appearance.bearing: Slow, deliberate, and constantly in motion below the shoulders. Above the collar she moves like a woman who has worked a shaft for twenty years. Below it, the hands are frequently doing something she did not start, and the thing she is best at in the world — reading which vessel her own qi is in — has become something that happens to her while she stands still. She has got so used to consulting herself that she has twice caught herself answering a question she was asked aloud.
appearance.pronouns: In this record, she and her and every feminine pronoun belong to the HOST, Nera Roke. The tendril layer is it, or the colony, or the layer, and it is never she — including in the passages where it is doing the deciding. This matters more here than in any other record of the pair, because the layer has no voice and its entire expressive range is the choice of meridian, so every sentence in this record about what it wants is a sentence about what the charge did. Where a passage reports the layer's preference it takes it and cites the route. Where a passage reports the host's decision it takes her.

canon.role_in_story:
A thornline colony has no gate, no ladder and no hands. It runs the pair's qi along vessels the host already owns, chooses which of the twelve the charge travels down, and stops at the liver because the tendril layer has no passage through a liver. That is the whole of its capability: it routes. And because it cannot speak and cannot open a gate of its own, routing is the only thing it has left, which makes the meridian itself its speech and its syntax — a sentence is a route, a correction is a reroute, and silence is the same route held until the charge runs out.

Nera Roke has been reading that grammar for twenty years. She is the only person in the record who can, because she is the only person who is inside the sentence, and the competence is not taught and cannot be checked from outside: no plate on the cleft can confirm a single route she reports, because every reading is taken through the body being read. Her gift and her disqualification are the same tendril layer, which is the standing condition of this whole species and is not news. What is new about her is what she did with twenty years of it.

She stopped asking which of them is deciding. That is the whole of her, and it is not a resignation, because the reroutes are better. The layer reads her qi at a resolution she cannot approach and when it moves a charge down a different vessel the technique improves — measurably, by the only measure that exists here, which is that the gate comes easier afterwards. So she has spent two decades obeying an opinion that is better than hers and expressed entirely in the movement of her own reserve, and she has never been able to establish whether it is correcting her or merely doing a better job.

And there is no way to ask. A colony answers the host's introspection, so the mind path is closed in the host's own right and she has no interior instrument to settle a question with; the thing that answers inside her is the party she would need to interrogate. Asking aloud is worse than useless: it produces a spoken answer in the host's voice, from the party whose opinion is in question, and she has heard herself give one twice. So the question is permanent, it is answerable by nothing in the setting, and she has organised her entire working life around not asking it out loud — which is why the record has her at the same shaft, on the same face, with the same load, twenty years on, and a scored line on her right forearm that she put there to mark a day she cannot date and still cannot explain.
canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as a correction. A cleft loading clerk logged four loads from the same face in one week that had been carried by a body whose technique did not match the shift's routine, and asked the miner to account for it. She gave the account. The account was correct in every particular and differed from her shift pattern at four points, all of them in the direction of a technique that was easier to do than the one she had been taught, and she did not know she was giving an account of a second party's routes because she had never had to tell the difference.
canon.lore:
The colony has no voice. It is a tendril layer threaded along the host's twelve ordinary meridians with a root cluster at the sternum and a fruiting node at the throat, it draws a small continuous fraction of the host's refined qi, and it goes exactly as far as the twelve go and no further. It seats no gate of its own and it climbs no ladder; every gate this pair has opened was opened by the host, on the host's throughput, along vessels the host already owned. What it can do — the one capability the biology gives it — is choose a route. It cannot take a gate the host cannot take. It cannot refuse the host a gate the host can take. It cannot, at any point, do anything at all except send the qi somewhere the host did not send it.

Which makes routing its entire expressive range, and twenty years has taught Nera Roke to read it the way she reads a face. A charge that arrives on the route she would have chosen is agreement. A charge that diverts mid-vessel is a correction, and she has learned which corrections are about her technique and which are about her timing. A route held open past the point where the charge would have run out is the closest thing the colony has to emphasis. A route that does not move at all, when it would have, is refusal, and in twenty years she has seen it refuse her exactly once, on a day she has never been able to reconstruct, and has no idea what she asked for.

And the routing is better than she is. This is the fact that everything else in her life is arranged around. The layer reads her qi field at a resolution she has no instrument for and cannot build, because every reading it takes runs along the same channels her qi runs along. When it moves a charge, the gate afterwards comes easier — not always, and not always soon, and never in a way she can reproduce on purpose — and she has never been able to distinguish between the layer correcting her and the layer being simply more efficient than she is. Both hypotheses predict twenty years of better technique. Nothing she owns separates them.

She cannot ask. Not because the colony refuses to answer — it has no capacity for answering, and asking is the one thing the arrangement makes impossible rather than merely difficult. A thornline answers the host's introspection, so the mind path is closed in the host's own right, which is the only liability in the bible that is inherited rather than authored: she did not choose it and she cannot give it up without dying. Her interior instrument is therefore the party whose opinion she would need to test. Asking aloud produces a spoken answer in her own voice, from the party in question, and she has twice caught herself in the middle of one and stopped. So the question is unanswerable by anything in the setting, permanently, and she has dealt with it the only way a body with no office and no standing can: she has stopped trying, and put her hands where the routes are, and gone back to work. The line scored across her right forearm is what is left of the one day the colony refused her, and she cut it to mark the occasion and cannot say what the occasion was.
history: Implanted at twenty, by the ordinary accident that is the only transmission route the species has: the spore is common, contagious, shed at the throat node and implanted directly, and it cannot be acquired deliberately, so every thornline in the setting exists because it happened to somebody by accident.

Finished developing inside a working body and, within three years, had begun to notice that her gates arrived easier when she had not practised them first, and did not have a word for what she was noticing.

Began routing as a discipline at twenty-six, after a bad year in which she tried to force a fourth gate and the layer walked the charge around the vessel twice and simply did not let it arrive. She has never forced anything since.

Stopped keeping a written account of her own practice at about thirty, on the reasoning that anything she wrote down would be a thing she could be asked to demonstrate, and there is no instrument on any tier that could demonstrate it.
Cut the line across her right forearm in a year she does not date, to mark the one occasion on which the colony refused her, and has never been able to reconstruct what she asked for.

Twenty years of a better opinion arriving through her own body has made her extremely good at not arguing with people she cannot see.

relationships.kind: the vessel her second party's sentences are written in
relationships.note: The one ordinary vessel whose work is bookkeeping rather than strength: it holds what the body has decided not to spend, and damage there does not cripple, it exhausts quietly and last, which is why it goes unreported for years. That description is the colony's speech exactly. It cannot open a gate, cannot refuse a gate the host can take, and cannot do anything except decide what the body does not yet spend — so the pair's whole range of expression is written in the bladder, and twenty years of reading it has taught Nera more about her own interior than any technique on the cleft could have.

relationships.kind: the only vessel in the record where the qi circles instead of sitting
relationships.note: Core formation gives the dantian a floor of its own, a core that qi circulates around rather than pools in, and the cost is comprehension rather than progress: the practitioner has to hold the circulation through an exhale, which is a skill and not a quantity. That is the only place in the setting where a body is built around motion rather than storage, and it is what the pair have without being taught it. Nera has spent two decades holding a circulation she was never instructed in, through an exhale, with the only evidence that it is being held correctly that the gate afterwards is easier.

relationships.kind: the body she is inside, and the reason any of it is legible
relationships.note: The hybrid is the one configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age, and it is treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it because the colony dies within the hour of the host and the pair cannot be separated for any examination without killing both. That is why Nera can read a route no external plate could confirm and can also never have that reading corroborated: the instrument and the subject are the same frame, and the frame's own hybrids are the only bodies in the record that carry this layer.

relationships.kind: the species that is both her habitat and the reason she is hunted
relationships.note: A thornline cannot finish developing outside a living body, so the ordinary population is the entire range. Every persecution the setting records against this species is a persecution of commonborn hosts for carrying something the commonborn did not choose, and no jurisdiction will hear it in a form that would be admitted, because a colony cannot be produced on request and the implantation is the one instant no office can schedule or witness. Nera's particular version of it is quieter: she is not the host's stigma on the shaft face, she is the reason the shaft face is three people short.

relationships.kind: the standing question of whether her body may be entered at all
relationships.note: The dispute runs on a colonized body and a mortuary college, and its prize is whether a body may be entered in the register at all; it cannot be split because the frame distinguishes the two parties by a colony that dies. Here the discriminator never fires, because the colony outlives nobody — it goes with the host within the hour — so the register's method finds one occupant where there are two, every time, and cannot be shown to be wrong. The register keeps the burnt list and reads the dead as the frame said, and the frame says one, and the body says two in every measurement anybody has ever taken of it.

relationships.kind: the only record in the setting made of things that were observed and not agreed
relationships.note: A pocket that presses fifteen imprints into one held value admits observers and has returned no two descriptions that agree, so its only surviving record is a list of disagreements, certified by nobody because a certified reading would let a vacant seat be argued filled. Nera's twenty years are the same kind of record and the same kind of custody: a private list of observations that cannot be sworn, held by the one person who has no standing to hold a record of any kind, on ground where concealment is the price of continuing to be left alone. Neither list is evidence. Both are the only copies.

reference_stats.combat_read: The host's body fights and the layer will reroute mid-action, so the pair fights as one thing with two opinions and the target is both halves — kill either and the other goes within the hour, which makes it a hostage situation from the first strike rather than a duel. Do not try to read her to predict her; every reading taken of her is taken through the body being read, and she is a better reader of it than you are. Do not separate them and do not attempt to address the layer directly, because the only channel it has runs through the host and comes out in the host's voice, which means anything you ask it you have asked her. Pressure the host instead: the loan is drawn continuously, empties on the host's schedule, and the layer's routing improves as the host tires rather than worsening, so fatigue makes her harder to predict and not easier. The one thing that reliably changes her behaviour is a gate she is about to open, because that is the one event she still takes personally.
notes: The closed path is the mind and it closes in the HOST's right, not the colony's. Write it that way in every summary, on pain of writing a parasite's opinion as a law.
Every her in this record is the host. The layer is it, or the colony, or the layer — including in the passages where it is the one deciding, which is most of them.

Her gift and her disqualification are the same tendril layer: she reads a meridian route better than any plate on the cleft and cannot be separated for the comparison that would make the reading count.

Routing is the colony's only expressive range. Never give it words, a voice, a gesture or a second register — the flattener out of the throat node is another body's habit, and this pair has never spent anything on sound.
The two-for-one structure is a legal floor: this body produces two dead and one bill, and every death, burial or save screen for the pair owes exactly that.

realm: The seventh gate, reached on the host's throughput and the layer's routing, and stalled there not by a shortage but because a tendril layer has no passage through a liver. name: Ansel Vantrel

appearance.presentation: Light, narrow-boned, deep and slow, with the long marrow and dense bone of her species and the minimal muscle that goes with them. She is not fragile and cannot be exhausted; she can be broken by force in a way she will take weeks to notice. Drawn at three-quarter on an approach road above the Scar, staff in one hand, spare sleeve tied at the elbow because the coat was cut for somebody a size larger forty years ago and never recut. Everything about her reads as storage: the wide flat bones of the hands, the visible ridge of the sternum, the unhurried way she puts one foot down after the other. Nothing about her reads as fast, because nothing about her has ever been.
appearance.age: Two hundred and seventy, which on the Starmetal Scar is very nearly nothing. This tier runs at five to fifty times a slower world's clock, so four centuries measured against a mortal's is a different quantity on every ground this body stands on, and the ground she chose is the one where her lifespan buys the least. She is the youngest member of her house by any margin and the only one who has ever complained about it, once, in writing, and then withdrawn the complaint.
appearance.build: Light to the point of fragility to force, with long dense bone and almost no muscle, standing on a frame that does not move much and recovers from anything it is asked to do at a rate nothing else in the record can approach. Her spine is the most heavily built thing about her and she uses it the way everyone else uses their hands: automatically, and for four hundred years. The bones are pale under the skin and the joints are visibly wide, and she has the loose unbothered carriage of somebody who has never once had to hurry.
appearance.complexion: Grey at the temples and then grey everywhere, with the papery dryness her species carries in its fourth century and a complexion that never flushes and never goes pale — she has been struck, cut and burned and has healed each time without the face ever showing it. The one thing that does show is the hairline of the shins, where forty years of exposed road have gone the colour of old ash, and the hands, which are the colour of wet stone and are always cold to the touch.
appearance.hair: White, cut once in this century, by herself, badly, with a knife meant for rope. It has grown out since into the asymmetry it always does, and she has declined to have it cut again by anyone else because the last person who did it asked her four questions about the approach that were, she noted, a survey. She keeps it tied off with the spare sleeve.
appearance.eyes: Dark, steady and slow to focus on anything that has moved in the last second, which is most things. Four centuries of looking at one subject from one fixed point has made her extraordinarily good at a gradient and indifferent to a face, and people who have not met her before tend to think she is not looking at them. She is looking at what they are standing on.
appearance.palette: Road grey, wet stone and the cold white of old bone across everything she owns, with one worn blue at the collar and cuffs of a coat that has been mended so many times the thread is a different colour from the cloth. No colour anywhere on her body. The only saturated thing in her picture is the metal of the staff head, which is star metal and which is the single object in the setting she has never let anybody else hold.
appearance.attire: A road coat cut for a larger woman, taken in twice and mended a third time, over a lined work jacket and a high collar that closes to the throat — which she insists on and which is not a matter of warmth, because her species does not feel cold and has never needed to. Thick boots resoled three times by somebody who was not asked, felted shin-wraps underneath, and a second pair of sleeves cut off at the elbow and carried tied at her belt for roads that will ruin the first pair. Everything on her is somebody else's alteration and has been for forty years.
appearance.marks: The scored shins from exposed road, symmetrical and useless as a record of anything except her own stubbornness. A healed break at the left radius that is the reason she carries the staff in her right hand and would rather not discuss it. And one mark that is not damage: a narrow band of skin at the inside of both wrists a shade paler than the rest, precisely the width of a road-cordon tie, which is where she has worn a band for two hundred years holding the two ends of her own reserve apart.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried to a degree that reads as indifference and is not. She stops before she turns and turns before she steps, so nothing she does surprises anybody, and the effect on a person walking with her is a peculiar pressure to slow down and match it. She stands with her weight even and her hands visible, which is a road habit she has never had cause to unlearn, and she has never once in four centuries been in a hurry to leave a place she has not finished looking at.

canon.role_in_story:
The Iron Vine hands out load and not edge, and every sworn member who holds no office is a Ward — the unbounded office, which recognises no stat at all, because what the house gives is load and load is not a stat. Ansel Vantrel is a Ward who has taken nothing for two hundred years, and the refusal is not austerity. It is a technique, and it is the only technique her body will accept.

A longmarrow keeps qi in bone marrow that turns over at about a percent a year and closes the body path outright, because hardening the bone stops the turnover the qi depends on. So there is no structural obstruction to any gate; no gate has ever refused her species, and there is no ceiling and no last rung. What there is instead is turnover, which is slow, so a gate is paid for out of tissue that arrives at a percent a year and takes about a century to assemble a lifetime's worth of. The store therefore refills rather than fills: it is the most reliable reservoir in the record, and every institution built around her species is built on the assumption that a longmarrow can be given things and will hold them indefinitely. She declines the giving, because a store that has been allowed to fill is a store whose oldest contents are older than the gate she is saving for, and a gate paid for entirely out of tissue that predates it is a gate she cannot reach on her own schedule.

Which puts her at the ninth after two hundred and seventy years, with the tenth booked for a date she is confident she will not see, on a ladder that has never refused her and never will. The whole of her cultivation is a deficit she maintains on purpose. She cultivates starved: no load, no gift, no reservoir carried past what the tissue can replace in a working lifetime, and every technique she runs is run thin. It is the discipline her species cannot practise, because the one technique that would let her bank regardless is the body path, and the body path stops the turnover the qi depends on, and a longmarrow who hardens their own bone suffocates on their own reserves within a decade.

The road above the Starmetal Scar is where she holds the claim. A resource that cannot be exhausted cannot be monopolised either, so the Scar is indefensible ground everybody must keep using, and the only durable claim on it is over the approach rather than the metal — which is the one thing left standing when every institution her species has ever founded has failed to survive the century that built it. She cannot fight, has never pretended she could, and does not need to: the approach is held by somebody who is always there and is never going anywhere, and the whole of her competence is that four centuries of looking at one subject has made her the most accurate reader of a road that exists.
canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as a refusal that was entered twice. A Warden clerk logged her as declining a full load of the house's finest store, noted the refusal as discipline, and then logged the same refusal for the following nine periods in the same terms, at which point the house changed the column and started recording her as a quantity of load not taken. The row exists because the house could not leave it out: a Ward who declines forever is not a member, and there is no office in the Iron Vine for a member who has taken nothing for two centuries.
canon.lore:
Everything this species is for and everything it cannot do is the same fact. A longmarrow keeps qi in bone marrow that turns over at roughly a percent a year, lives four centuries on it, and closes the body path outright, because hardening the bone stops the turnover the qi depends on — which is why the longest-lived body in the record is built out of the one material it may never stop replacing. The consequence is not a ceiling. There is no ceiling: no gate has ever refused a longmarrow, the ladder has no last rung in front of her, and the densest bodies on any tier stop at seventeen while she has no reason at all to stop anywhere. The limitation is entirely downstream of the success. Turnover is slow, so everything is slow; a gate is paid for out of tissue that arrives at a percent a year, and nothing she does is a matter of progress so much as of attrition.

So her species has one enormous advantage and one prohibition. The advantage is that the store renews instead of filling: a reservoir that is replaced rather than topped up can be given anything and will not empty, which is the arrangement the Iron Vine was built to exploit, and it is why every institution around her species is an institution of give. The prohibition is that the discipline which would let her bank regardless — the body path, which hardens the very tissue the store runs on — is closed to her by that same tissue, and a longmarrow who takes it suffocates on their own reserves inside a decade. The pair is exact and neither half is negotiable, and it is the only place in the setting where the strongest thing about a body and the thing forbidden to it are the same organ.

Ansel has spent two centuries resolving that pair by refusing the advantage. Load, which the house hands out and which most of her species would hold indefinitely, makes the store's contents older. A store that has been filled is a store whose oldest layer predates the gate being saved for, and a gate funded mostly from tissue that existed before the decision to climb is a gate reached on somebody else's arithmetic rather than her own. So she keeps the reserve thin — deliberately, permanently, and by the only route available to her, which is declining. It is a subtraction maintained for two hundred years by not accepting anything, in a house whose entire product is accepting. And the discipline she is running is therefore starved: every technique she uses, she uses thin, on a reserve that is never more than a working lifetime deep, which is why nine gates have taken two hundred and seventy years and why the tenth is a date rather than a plan.

There is a second reason she does not leave, and it is the setting's rather than her own. The Starmetal Scar is a wound on the Immortal Court that keeps healing, on the one tier whose clock runs five to fifty times slower, so a resource that cannot be exhausted cannot be monopolised either, and the only durable claim anyone holds over it is a claim on the approach. The approach is four days of bad road. She cannot fight and has never pretended she could, and this ground does not reward pretending: it rewards somebody who will still be standing at the head of it in a century, and four centuries is not long here. Everything her species ever founded failed to survive the century that built it, because a body that cannot harden cannot leave anything durable behind — so the one durable thing left for a body like hers is a road, held by sitting on it. She has held this one for two hundred years. Nobody has ever relieved her and nobody has ever been able to, because relief would require somebody who intends to stay.
history: Entered the Iron Vine as a sworn member at nineteen and was made a Ward inside a decade, which is the shortest anyone in her house's history has held the unbounded office and which surprised people who later found out she was the youngest rather than the most capable.

Took her first load at twenty-six and spent forty years running on it, and concluded — from the age of the tissue at the bottom of her own reserve rather than from any instruction — that a filled store funds gates on somebody else's arithmetic.
Declined the second load in the sixtieth year and has declined every one since, which took the house some decades to accept and which the house has never once discussed with her directly.

Came to the Scar's approach at about seventy and has not left it in two centuries, holding the claim on the road rather than on the metal, because the metal cannot be exhausted and so cannot be owned.
Booked the tenth gate for a date she is confident she will not see, and wrote it down anyway, and has told nobody what she will do if she reaches it, including herself.

personality.summary: Enormously patient and completely immovable, and the two are the same disposition rather than one covering the other. She declines things without embarrassment and without a speech, walks at the speed of somebody who knows the road will still be here, and asks people fewer questions than they expect because she has usually already read the answer off the ground they are standing on.

personality.voice: Unhurried, plain and short, in the register her house uses for arithmetic rather than for argument. She uses no metaphor and no courtesy formula, says the number first and the reason second, and has a habit of ending a sentence with a date. There is no second register in her speech and nothing in it varies: the most she has ever done in public is stop talking for a year, which the house logged as a quantity of silence not supplied.
